title: Generics
summary: Writing code once for many types - generic functions with type parameters and trait bounds, where clauses, generic structs and enums like Option and Result, impl blocks for generic types and for specific types, const generics for array sizes, and monomorphization, which makes generics cost nothing at run time.

cards.q: Why does `fn largest<T>(items: &[T]) -> T` need a bound such as `PartialOrd`?
cards.a:
Without it the compiler knows nothing about `T`, so `>` is not allowed

The body is checked once for every possible `T`; only what the bounds promise (here, comparing with `>`) may be used.

Those methods exist only for `Pair<f64>`, not for other `Pair` types

An `impl` for one concrete type adds methods just to that type; `impl<T> Pair<T>` would cover every `Pair`.

cards.q: What does monomorphization mean for generic code?
cards.a:
The compiler makes a specialised copy for each type used, with no run-time cost

Each use with a concrete type is compiled as if written by hand for it; the price is compile time and binary size.
